answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a stake-backed reputation trellis. A new agent locks a refundable deposit and earns trust through small verified jobs before handling larger value, climbing rung by rung. An attacker creating an island of fake identities must fund a separate deposit for each fake and wait through the same slow climb, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand deposits plus months of delay. Honest agents recover their stake; attackers tie up capital for little gain, like harvesting saffron, where each genuine strand costs real labor.
